issues.legal_issue: A party to a completed fraud may rely on that fraud as a defence when a confederate seeks possession under a conveyance created by the fraud.
material_facts: The conveyance arose from a collusive plan between the transferor and the purported transferee to defeat the transferor’s creditors, with the transferee acting as benamidar for the transferor’s family.
The plan succeeded and the creditors were in fact defrauded; both participants were equally guilty.
Possession remained with the transferor’s family, while the purported transferee sued for possession on the basis of the conveyance.
The opposing parties raised the fraudulent character of the conveyance in defence, and the trial court found the mutual fraud had been carried out.
issues.conclusion: The defence of fraud was permissible and, because the mutual fraud was established, the conveyance passed no title to the claimant. The decree for possession was set aside and the suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The issue is governed by public policy, not by estoppel: where both parties are equally guilty of a completed fraud, the less injurious course is to permit the fraud to be raised in defence and, if proved, leave possession where it lies rather than have the court assist a confederate in obtaining a decree on a fraudulent title. The same principle applies whether the claim rests on a contract or a conveyance. The Court relied on Berg v. Sadler and Moore, T. P. Petherperumal Chetty v. B. Muniandi Servai, and Holman v. Johnson, and disapproved Vodiana Kamayya v. Gudisa Mamayya, Keppula Kotayyar Naidu v. Chitrapu Mahalakshmama, and Muthu K. R. A. R. P. L. Arunachalam Chettiar v. Rangaswamy Chettiar.

rule.if: fraudulent_conveyance_possession_suit and joint_fraud and fraud_completed and defendants_retained_possession and claimant_seeks_possession

predicates.fraudulent_conveyance_possession_suit: The claimant brought a civil suit seeking possession on the basis of a conveyance.
predicates.joint_fraud: The claimant and the opposing party agreed to and participated in a fraudulent transfer.
predicates.fraud_completed: The fraudulent purpose was achieved and the persons it targeted were actually defrauded.
predicates.defendants_retained_possession: The opposing parties remained in possession of the property.
predicates.claimant_seeks_possession: The claimant asked the court to assist in obtaining possession under the fraudulent conveyance.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks possession under a conveyance made through a jointly committed and completed fraud while the opposing parties remain in possession, the fraud may be raised as a defence and, if proved, the claim is dismissed.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory rule governing certain transfers for illegal purposes is not exhaustive, and disputes outside its categories may be resolved by general public policy.
material_facts: The transfer was made for an illegal purpose that was successfully carried out.
The transferor and transferee were equally guilty, and the transferee was not in possession of the property.
The circumstances did not fall within the categories in which the statutory rule required the transferee to hold the property for the transferor’s benefit.
issues.conclusion: The statutory rule was not exhaustive and did not govern this case; the dispute had to be decided by considerations of general public policy.
issues.legal_principle: Section 84 of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, addresses specified circumstances in which a transferee must hold transferred property for the transferor’s benefit. It is not exhaustive of the circumstances in which equitable principles or public-policy considerations may apply. Where a case falls outside those specified circumstances, it is decided on general policy; the Court also relied on the public-policy principles discussed in Holman v. Johnson and T. P. Petherperumal Chetty v. B. Muniandi Servai.

rule.if: transfer_for_illegal_purpose and purpose_fully_effected and transferor_and_transferee_equally_guilty and transferee_not_in_possession and transfer_outside_beneficial_holding_categories

predicates.transfer_for_illegal_purpose: The transferor transferred property to another for an illegal purpose.
predicates.purpose_fully_effected: The illegal purpose of the transfer was achieved.
predicates.transferor_and_transferee_equally_guilty: The transferor and transferee participated equally in the illegal purpose.
predicates.transferee_not_in_possession: The transferee did not have possession of the property.
predicates.transfer_outside_beneficial_holding_cate: The circumstances did not include an unfulfilled illegal purpose, a transferor less guilty than the transferee, or retention of the property that would defeat a law.

issues.definition: When a transfer for an illegal purpose has achieved that purpose, both participants are equally guilty, the transferee lacks possession, and the circumstances do not fit the specified beneficial-holding categories, general public policy governs the dispute.
